data.name: Maheshkumar
data.gender_notes: Maheshkumar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Maheshkumar is a compound name derived from the words Mahesh and Kumar. Mahesh is a name for Lord Shiva, the Hindu god of the mountains, and Kumar refers to a young man or a god in a youthful form. The name thus symbolizes the god of the mountains being compassionate towards his devotees. The name Maheshkumar carries the meaning “God of the Mountain (Mahesh) + Compassionate (Kumar)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Maheshkumar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the mountain (mahesh) + compassionate (kumar) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine compassion and protection.
data.etymology: Maheshkumar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the Mountain (Mahesh) + Compassionate (Kumar).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maheshkumar total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: The name 'Maheshkumar' is a combination of two Sanskrit words: 'Mahesh' (meaning 'great lord', a name for Shiva) and 'Kumar' (meaning 'young prince'). This name was used to denote Shiva as the young god with great power and authority.

The 'Maheshkumar' form of Shiva is also associated with the 'Maheshwara' form, which is considered as the ruler of the universe. During the Medieval period, this name was popularly used in various Hindu temples and scriptures to denote Shiva as the supreme god and the ultimate ruler of the universe.
